newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1997 growth seen hitting 5.7 pct - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1997 growth seen hitting 5.7 pct - JP Morgan.

text.p: Mexico's gross domestic product could grow 5.7 percent in 1997, up from a previously forecast 4.3 percent, J.P. Morgan said in a report.
GDP rose 7.6 percent in the last quarter of 1996 year-over-year, the biggest quarterly gain since 1981, the government said last week.
The seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter increase was 4.2 percent.

"The end-1996 result makes clear that growth is now set to remain high during 1997, and warrants lifting of the forecast full-year outcome from 4.3 percent to 5.7 percent," J.P. Morgan's Mexico City office said.
